title: Hand-held Power-free Microfluidic Device for Droplet Generation
author: Chen, Wu, et al.

steps.title: Prepare SU-8 mold
steps.instruction: Fabricate a microstructure mold on a 4‑inch silicon wafer using SU‑8 to a height of 120 µm by photolithography, then silanize the mold before use.

steps.title: Place mold in petri dish
steps.instruction: Leave the silanized mold in a 5‑inch Petri dish with the micro‑features facing up.

steps.title: Mix and degas PDMS
steps.instruction: Mix 50 g of PDMS (curing agent : polymer base at 2 : 10) for 3 min. Pour 40 g of the mixture onto the SU‑8 mold and the remaining PDMS onto another 4‑inch Petri dish. Place both dishes in a desiccator and apply vacuum for 5 min until all bubbles disappear.

steps.title: Cure PDMS
steps.instruction: Transfer the Petri dishes to an oven and cure the PDMS at 70 °C for 30 min.

steps.title: Demold and punch ports
steps.instruction: Score the cured PDMS around the circumference, peel it off the mold, and with the featured side up punch inlet ports with a 3 mm hole punch and an outlet port with a 1.5 mm punch. Ensure the PDMS slab is at least 3 mm thick and that all holes are completely clear; practice on dummy PDMS to avoid cracks.

steps.title: Wash PDMS specimens
steps.instruction: Sonicate the PDMS pieces in 1 : 100 diluted dish detergent for 10 min, replace with DI water and sonicate twice more. Keep specimens fully immersed, never overlapping, and wear powder‑free gloves.

steps.title: Dry PDMS specimens
steps.instruction: Blow‑dry the washed PDMS specimens using purified, compressed air.

steps.title: Plasma activate PDMS
steps.instruction: Place the PDMS in a plasma chamber with the featured side up, evacuate to 1 torr, and activate plasma for 1 min.

steps.title: Bond PDMS layers
steps.instruction: Carefully place the 3‑mm thick PDMS (features down) onto the flat PDMS piece, then incubate at 70 °C for 3 h to achieve bonding.

steps.title: Punch holes in collection vial
steps.instruction: Use a 3 mm hole punch to make two holes in the silicone septum of the sample collection vial.

steps.title: Insert tubing into vial
steps.instruction: Insert two 15‑cm Tygon tubings (A and B) through the holes; position tubing A so ~1 cm of it lies inside the vial and tubing B so its tip touches the vial bottom. Apply epoxy seal if needed.

steps.title: Add oil to collection vial
steps.instruction: Load 100 µL of droplet‑generating oil into the collection vial.

steps.title: Seal collection vial
steps.instruction: Screw the cap onto the vial, ensuring the oil does not leak.

steps.title: Attach needle and syringe
steps.instruction: Insert a 19 G blunt needle into the outer end of tubing A and connect the needle to a 10 mL syringe.

steps.title: Print and prepare station
steps.instruction: 3D‑print the station from PLA (CAD file available on request).

steps.title: Cut droppers for reservoirs
steps.instruction: Cut the bulb of three plastic droppers to a remaining height of 5 mm to serve as reservoirs, and cut the straw part to a remaining length of 2 mm to act as inserts for the PDMS chip; cut inserts at an angle close to, but not exactly, 90° to avoid flow blockage. (200 µL pipette tips may be used but are not recommended because they trap air).

steps.title: Assemble reservoirs and test airtightness
steps.instruction: Insert all reservoirs into the inlet ports and tubing B into the outlet port; optionally apply a thin layer of silicone glue at each junction. To verify airtightness, load 100 µL water into each of the three reservoirs, pull the syringe plunger to the 10 mL tick quickly, then release; water should not leak and the plunger should return to its initial position within a few seconds.

steps.title: Set syringe to 7 mL
steps.instruction: Pull the syringe plunger to the 7.0 mL tick.

steps.title: Load aqueous solution A
steps.instruction: Load 100 µL of aqueous solution A into reservoir 1.

steps.title: Load aqueous solution B
steps.instruction: Load 100 µL of aqueous solution B into reservoir 2.

steps.title: Load oil into reservoir
steps.instruction: Load 150 µL of droplet‑generating oil into reservoir 3 (follow steps 6‑8 sequentially to minimize droplet size variation).

steps.title: Set syringe to 9 mL and rest
steps.instruction: Pull the syringe plunger quickly to the 9.0 mL tick and rest the syringe on the station, holding the plunger in position with the fixture.

steps.title: Stop flow by unscrewing vial
steps.instruction: After 40 s of flow, unscrew the collection‑vial cap; breaking the vacuum stops the flow. Extending the flow time leads to inconsistent droplet sizes.

steps.title: Collect generated droplets
steps.instruction: Collect droplets from the top layer of the collection vial (droplet‑generating oil is heavier than the droplets); approximately 150 000 droplets are generated within this timeframe.

description: The system was validated by two settings. First setting is designed to encapsulate aqueous solution mixed with green food grade dye for better visualization; second setting is designed to encapsulate magnetic beads (30 μm, 350 bead/μL) for single cell sequencing feasibility test. (Beads and cells have higher density than water and tend to sediment in the reservoirs and result in flow blockage. We have developed a method to mitigate this issue and will discuss in future publication) Fig. 2 shows that the droplets being formed in the chip and flow throw the tubing into the collection vial. Fig. 3 shows time-lapse images of droplet formation from the beginning of the flow untill 28 s after flow started, with 100,000 droplets generated. Fig. 4 shows solution in the collection vial contains droplets with high size consistency. 20-μL aliquots from multiple locations of the collection vial were acquired, spread on a glass slide and imaged right away. The droplet size was analyzed using ImageJ (an open source software). The average size of the droplets is 109 μm, with standard deviation of 9 μm (CV < 8%).Fig. 2Step-by-step workflow. a) Set up the system. Droplets composed with an aqueous solution with magnetic beads and another aqueous solution are formed at the junction.
